partner.result_used: For every invertible indefinite original-coordinate physical triple S, its majority/one-sheet output submeasure is dominated by C_S dx for arbitrary rough cap-one product laws and arbitrary outside couplings; C_S is the exact ruled constant and C_S<=pi*sqrt(2)/sigma_min(A_SS).

new_results.statement: For every probability measure mu on R, D_inf(mu)=sup_{0<eps<=1} ||mu*gamma_eps||_infinity, where D_inf is the least C with mu<=C dx, extended by infinity. No prior absolute continuity or continuity is required.
mu has a C_0 density iff mu*gamma_eps converges in L-infinity as eps->0; this cleanly separates continuity from bounded density.
With s(A)=s_3(A), sup_target s(A)D_inf(mu_Q)=sup_target s(A)||mu_Q*gamma_1||_infinity, by exact spectral scaling.
For an invertible indefinite original-coordinate triple S, Q-c_S(W)=(1/4)g_S^T A_SS^{-1}g_S with g=grad Q, hence the majority event is {g_S^T adj(A_SS)g_S<=0}.

If nonnegative weights a_S on indefinite physical triples satisfy sum_S a_S 1_{g_S^T adj(A_SS)g_S<=0}>=1 for every g in range(A), then mu_Q(E)<=|E| sum_S a_S C_S and ||p_Q||_infinity<=sum_S a_S C_S. At a Gaussian heat posterior nu, H_eps(y) E_nu[sum_S a_S1_GS]<=sum_S a_SC_S.
